newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST - HK newspaper headlines - Nov 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - HK newspaper headlines - Nov 28.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Thursday. Reuter has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- MING PAO DAILY -- Manufacturers attacked the issue of high land prices during a Selection Committee question-and-answer session for the three Chief Executive candidates.

-- Eight parties in China started re-electing their leaders, which would be completed before the 15th general conference of the Communist Party next year. It said the Communist Party had instructed that the new leadership should be younger and the age of chairmans should not exceed 80.

-- TA KUNG PAO -- Three candidates for Chief Executive gave impressive performances at the quizzing by the 400 members of the Selection Committee, and the 63 questions put forward by the commercial and fiancial sectors covered extensive ground.
-- WEN WEI PO -- Chinese President Jiang Zemin starts a three-day visit to India on Thursday and would sign an agreement on measures to establish mutual trust on military matters.
-- APPLE DAILY -- A father and a son were detained for extorting $5.5 million by stealing bank account information from other people's mail boxes.

-- SING TAO DAILY -- Many drug rehabilitation centres on the mainland had become drug-taking centres because of a lack of government control. In one centre in Guizhou province, drugs were sold openly to addicts and even managers took drugs. When questioned, they said it helped to create a "relaxed" environment for the patients.
-- HONG KONG ECONOMIC TIMES -- Dickson Concepts confirmed that it intended to acquire the New York-based fashion chain store Barneys.

-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- Bankruptcies were expected to double in China this year as more enterprises bow out of financial woes before a new bankruptcy law is promulgated. An economist said there would be about 5,000 bankruptcy cases this year.
-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- Hong Kong's trade negotiators are putting the final touches on a shopping list they will take to the World Trade Organisation's ministers' conference next month.
-- China will establish a company to supply Taiwan shippers, signalling that direct links between the two rivals might be imminent.
